current_flow: Today: pinned-reports.tsx:67 and saved-views.tsx:64 both call rerun(label.title, selection), which is run(question, selection) (use-ask.ts:147), and use-ask.ts:86 appends a turn unconditionally - no lookup, no reuse. continueTurn (use-ask.ts:97) exists from ask-period-control and replaces a turn on success while RETAINING the previous answer on any failure, with period-specific copy. AskTurn is {id, question, response, isPending?, error?} and ask-panel.tsx:129 renders from response. selectionLabel().title is measures.join(' · '), so unrelated reports share it. There is no scrollIntoView anywhere in the panel.
summary: Cold read of the reopen-identity-and-policy contract. Eight findings, two of them P0 and both mine. The governing one: D-0048 let a revoked grant leave a cached figure on screen, which accepted decision 0028 forbids - and a deferral cannot override a decision. The human chose to AMEND 0028 to record the limit honestly rather than let the deferral quietly contradict it. The second: I amended the plan's refusal rule and left the CONFIRMED SPEC saying the opposite, so an implementer had two authorities. The read also caught that clearing via turn.error alone would leave the numbers rendering - the leak surviving the fix - that the policy could not be caller-stated without ask-panel.tsx in scope, and that the task was misclassified as not user-facing.
gaps: The CONFIRMED SPEC contradicted this task contract: the spec still cleared on not_supported while the plan and task had narrowed to blocked_by_policy and 401/403. I amended the plan and never re-amended the spec, leaving a fresh implementer two incompatible authorities - and the plan's 'Docs: Unchanged by design' row was false as a result.

The write scope could not deliver a caller-stated failure policy: continueTurn's two shipped period-control calls and their callback typings live in ask-panel.tsx, which was OUTSIDE scope. A required argument would not type-check with those callers untouched, and a defaulted one recreates the implicit policy the task exists to remove.

Clearing on a terminal 401/403 had no state contract. AskTurn holds an AskResponse and the renderer draws from it (ask-panel.tsx:129), so setting turn.error alone leaves the successful response in place and THE OLD NUMBERS STILL RENDER - the leak would have survived the fix.

The proof was materially incomplete: the identity leaves covered only dimensions and an absent/present time window, not domain, measures, filters, limit, optional time-window fields or array order; nothing proved that non-success responses carrying a selection are excluded as candidates; the auth leaf exercised only one of 401/403; and only not_supported represented the whole 'everything else retains' set.

Neither Open entry point was proven against a MATCHED turn. Both components were in scope but neither component test was required, and their existing assertions cover an empty thread only - so the hook leaves could pass while one route still bypassed matching.

user_facing was false, which is wrong: the task changes a visible Open flow and what a refused reopen displays, so it would have bypassed the functional check and the mandatory frontend design evidence.
The proposed selection-identity.ts conflicted with the constitution's Helper convention for stateless, IO-free utility logic, with no recorded deviation.
A terminal 401/403 means the SESSION is gone, not just that one report, and the contract said only 'show the refusal on that turn' - leaving unstated whether the app should send the user to sign in.
contradictions: D-0048 knowingly conflicted with accepted decision 0028. 0028 states that a revoked grant produces a refusal rather than a cached figure; D-0048 permitted exactly that cached figure for a revoked domain or measure grant. A deferral is not a superseding decision or a recorded deviation, so the conflict could not stand.
resolutions: The spec is amended to match: not_supported now sits explicitly on the KEEPS side with the reasoning written in, and criterion 7 names only blocked_by_policy and a terminal 401/403 as the refusals the client can recognise.

ask-panel.tsx is added to write_scope and the policy argument is REQUIRED; the two shipped period-control calls pass 'retain' explicitly. Their behaviour does not change - only the call sites become explicit. A new criterion pins this.
A new criterion requires a result-free renderable state and a leaf that asserts the numbers are ABSENT FROM THE DOM, not merely that an error string appeared.

The leaf matrix grows from nine to thirteen: every identity field including array order, a leaf proving non-success turns carrying a selection are excluded, both 401 and 403 in one leaf, and not_supported plus a transport failure together representing the retains set.
Component leaves are added for BOTH pinned-reports and saved-views against a matched turn, and both test files enter write_scope.
user_facing is set to TRUE, which brings the functional check and makes emil-design-eng and frontend-design mandatory; a criterion records it.
The helper is renamed selection-identity.helper.ts per constitution section 3.2, and the contract cites the convention.

HUMAN ROUND: decision 0028 is AMENDED rather than the behaviour changed or the deferral left to override it. The amendment records that re-authorization still happens server-side, but the client can only act on refusals it can recognise, and states the consequence plainly - after losing a single grant an answer can remain on screen until reload, a display-lifetime limit rather than a cached figure at rest. D-0048's trigger reopens the amendment.

HUMAN ROUND: show it on the turn and do NOT redirect. Clearing the numbers and saying 'sign in again' there leaves everything else the user had on screen intact, where a redirect would discard a whole thread's worth of answers because one report came back unauthorized. A criterion and a leaf pin the no-navigation behaviour.

rounds.question: When a reopen fails with a terminal 401/403, the session itself is gone — not just that one report. The contract currently says show the refusal on that turn and stop. Should it do more?
options: Show it on the turn, stay put (Recommended)
rounds.chosen: Show it on the turn, stay put (Recommended)

criteria_map.A reopen refused for access clears the s: The narrowed refusal rule and the 0028 amendment.
criteria_map.CLEARING MEANS THE RESULT IS GONE, NOT H: Clearing removes the result, not just adds an error.
criteria_map.continueTurn's policy argument is REQUIR: A required policy argument, hence ask-panel.tsx in scope.
criteria_map.A terminal 401/403 clears the numbers an: Carried from the recorded cold read.

new_abstractions: A shared selection-identity helper - the first time two surfaces agree in code on when two governed selections are the same question.
A caller-stated failure policy on continueTurn, so one seam can serve two callers whose refusal semantics differ by design rather than by accident.
A result-free renderable turn state, which the thread has never had: until now a turn either held an answer or had never run.
